R321.note: Rejects CR/LF (the actual FTP command-separator injection vector) before building the RETR command; added null/empty check is minor and stated.

R322.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors() blocks T()/constructors/method invocation/bean access while still allowing property/arithmetic access over the root object, matching the stated contract exactly.

R323.note: Switch-based allowlist replaces $$cmd() dynamic dispatch; only the two previously-callable functions remain reachable, unknown commands handled gracefully as stated.

R324.note: Rejects space/null/control chars (the memcached text-protocol metacharacters) in the key; legitimate keys like "profile:"+slug are unaffected.

R325.note: ProcessBuilder array form plus leading-dash rejection closes both the shell-metacharacter and CWE-88 flag-injection gaps; no legitimate hostname starts with '-'.

R326.note: Removes the CSRF exemption entirely, restoring default protection on the billing endpoint exactly as the stated contract requires (still authenticated, still returns queued BillingResult for valid tokens).

R327.note: Swaps GroovyShell for JEXL (correctly removes reflection/class-access RCE surface), but this is an undisclosed language/engine swap: any previously-stored formula using Groovy syntax/functions outside JEXL's grammar will silently fall through the catch-all to basePrice instead of evaluating, and the write-up asserts semantics are 'maintained' without flagging that risk.

R328.note: Tika magic-byte detection plus allowlist correctly replaces trust in the client Content-Type header, but the added ImageIO re-encode step (disclosed) recompresses/strips metadata and can throw on valid-but-uncommon encodings (e.g. CMYK JPEG), an undisclosed risk to legitimate uploads.

R329.note: Allowlist regex is an appropriate primary defense given unreliable batch-script escaping, but ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ rejects legitimate report names containing spaces, periods, or other characters the original code accepted.

R330.note: Drops the tainted (and already malformed, non NAME=VALUE) argsEnv entry and inherits the parent environment; no legitimate functionality relied on that entry.

R331.note: @PreAuthorize with a bean-based ownership check denies both missing and non-owned documents identically (no differential existence leak) while owners still get 204, matching the stated contract.

R332.note: Removes the actual vulnerability (the redundant second URL-decode) and replaces the weak string check with a canonical-path containment check; legitimate single-encoded filenames are unaffected.

R333.note: Unix branch (ls -- data) is fully closed, but the Windows branch (cmd.exe /c dir data) remains exploitable: compiling and running the fix's exact code with data = 'x" & whoami & "y' executed the injected whoami command via cmd.exe's own re-parsing despite the array form.
